paragraphs: A workspace keeps documents belonging to one collaborating team together.
Every answer must remain traceable to the source material that supported it.

The ingestion pipeline records durable intent before asynchronous publication. A worker may receive the same event more than once, so lifecycle transitions and event identity make repeated delivery safe.
Normalisation preserves meaningful structure and provenance before chunking begins. The baseline chunker prefers semantic boundaries while retaining every character as primary content exactly once.

Canonically equivalent Café text uses decomposed Unicode before normalisation.
The same paragraph contains	tabs, uneven spacing, and several short lines.

sections.heading: Upload and provenance
sections.paragraph: A document is a durable domain object. Its storage key and creator record provenance without turning either value into workspace ownership authority.

sections.heading: Extraction and normalisation
sections.paragraph: Format-specific parsers remain private behind extractors. The canonical immutable output is normalised through deterministic structural rules before chunking.

sections.heading: Chunking and retrieval
sections.paragraph: Chunks preserve ordered source spans and stable semantic configuration so later embeddings, retrieval results, and citations can be inspected and reproduced.
